name: Caesar
overview: Caesar, specifically Tiberius Caesar, was the Roman emperor during the time of Jesus' ministry. He was a male figure of authority referenced in Scripture, notably in Matthew 22:17 and Luke 3:1. His role is significant as the reigning imperial power during a pivotal period in biblical history.
namesAndTitles: The title 'Caesar' is used in Scripture as a designation of imperial authority and is not a personal name given by God. The specific reference to 'Tiberius Caesar' identifies the emperor during the early first century, confirming the historical context of Jesus' ministry. Neither name carries a Hebrew or Greek meaning beyond its status as a title.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Caesar beyond what is noted in his titles and historical identity. There are no familial connections detailed in the biblical text related to this figure.
scriptureSignificance: Caesar's significance in the biblical narrative lies in his position as the ruling emperor during Jesus' earthly ministry, providing the political backdrop for many events. His authority is indirectly acknowledged in the Gospels, emphasizing the interaction between earthly government and divine purpose. The mention of Caesar situates the Gospel accounts within a real historical framework, demonstrating God's sovereignty over all rulers.
